## TL;DR

The drawer QA pass found no reproducible product defect in the reviewed states. The durable QA note records the fixture matrix, viewport measurements, tab navigation checks, and the limitation around independently confirming auth-disabled server mode. The prior handoff failed at `ui-smoke`; in this continuation I ran the requested changed-path check successfully and then rebuilt/ran the UI smoke command directly. The smoke test passed after waiting for the shared Playwright slot, so the failure did not reproduce and no source change was justified.

## Work and rationale

I first verified the worktree, branch, current RepoOS task state, and the task’s review report. The task was active in the board even though the local task file retained its previous review bookkeeping state. The review report was still relevant and had no requested code changes; its verdict was “good to go,” with the QA note as the only substantive artifact. The worktree began clean.

The previous handoff message named `ui-smoke` as the failing step, but did not include the underlying smoke output. I ran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` as required. It completed successfully. RepoOS classified the current branch diff as documentation and task bookkeeping only, so build, test, and UI smoke stages were intentionally skipped in that scoped run. This meant that a green scoped check alone could not establish whether the earlier smoke failure had cleared.

To investigate that gate directly, I ran `bun run build && bun run smoke`. The build reported that the current build was up to date. UI smoke waited in the shared Playwright queue, then reported “Checks tabs passed at 1440, 390 and 320px in light and dark mode” and “UI smoke test passed.” The failure was therefore not reproducible on this run. The observed delay was slot contention, not a drawer assertion failure. No product-code change was needed to address it.

The existing QA note remains the report of the browser pass: seven drawer fixtures were checked at 1280×900 and 375×900, the drawer aligned to the viewport at both sizes, drawer tabs fit and navigated, and no horizontal overflow or browser errors were observed. It also explicitly states that the server startup printed `Preview auth.enabled`, so auth-disabled mode was not independently confirmed. I have preserved that qualification rather than upgrading it into a claim that the browser session proved auth was disabled. No destructive close-out action was run.

## Approaches tried

I inspected the task specification, the durable QA note, the prior review report, RepoOS handoff status, and the changed-path check output. I searched the worktree’s RepoOS logs for a preserved detailed smoke error; the task-specific log named in the search was not present, and the system log only exposed routine task API traffic. Since there was no recorded stack trace to diagnose, I reran the smoke gate from the current built app instead of guessing at a code fix.

I also considered whether to add a runtime or test change solely to force the smoke step into the scoped check. That would not address a reproduced defect: the branch’s current diff is bookkeeping-only, and the direct smoke test passed. I therefore kept the branch focused on the already reviewed QA documentation rather than introducing unrelated code or changing the check plan.

## Challenges and blockers

The handoff failure did not preserve its detailed command output in the available task-specific logs, which limited root-cause analysis of that exact run. The direct rerun provides evidence that the smoke test passes now, but cannot establish why the earlier attempt failed. Playwright queue contention added a short wait; the command completed successfully once its slot became available.

One acceptance detail remains qualified in the QA note: the prior browser session did not independently establish that the server was running with auth disabled because its startup output included `Preview auth.enabled`. The UI was browsed without encountering a sign-in prompt, but that alone is not sufficient evidence to claim the auth configuration was disabled. No new browser session was started during this continuation. This limitation is reported transparently rather than being represented as verified.

## Key learnings

Changed-path checks can correctly skip browser smoke on a bookkeeping-only diff. When a previous handoff names a skipped gate, run that gate directly so a green check does not conceal an unexamined failure. In this case the direct rerun passed; the only observed wait was the shared Playwright queue. Keep QA evidence precise about what was measured, which fixtures were used, and which server configuration was not independently confirmed.
